title: Heatmap-based SSE/WebSocket load prober with KV-cache priming and backpressure injection
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: build a scalable, chaos-resilient load testing harness for streaming chat/completions (SSE + WebSocket) that focuses on per-connection heatmaps, tokens/sec measurements, p95 token latency tracking, and automated regression detection. This harness will be used by runtime and infra teams to validate changes to batching, KV cache priming, kernel selection heuristics, and fallback routing policies.

Goals: 
- Provide a client-side simulator that reproduces realistic chat traffic mixes (short-turn, long-turn, multi-msg turns) and outputs per-connection heatmaps (connections x time) for concurrency and token emission patterns.
- Measure tokens/sec (aggregate and per-connection), first-byte and per-token p95/p99 latencies, and end-to-end session completion times.
- Include configurable KV-cache priming modes so the harness can exercise cold-start, warmed-prefix and partially-warmed KV-cache paths.
- Implement backpressure injection (slow consumer, TCP window throttling emulation, delayed reads) to observe queuing/backlog behavior and worst-case p95 regressions.
- Integrate regression detection: compare daily runs against a rolling baseline, compute effect size, and open alerts/PRs when p95 tokens/sec drops >10% with statistical significance.
- Produce dashboards and exportable artifacts (CSV/Parquet) for offline analysis and root-cause correlation with runtime traces.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Harness can generate 200k concurrent simulated stream connections across a sharded driver cluster while sustaining 3M tokens/sec synthetic throughput on a staging runtime cluster.
- Heatmap artifact generated per-run and visualized in Grafana (heatmap panel) with annotated phases (priming, steady-state, chaos injection).
- p95 token latency computed per-model and per-region; CI gating that fails if p95 increases by >15% versus baseline for two consecutive runs.
- KV-cache priming scenarios: cold, warm-prefix (N=5 tokens), warmed-KV (full KV preloaded). Per-scenario comparison artifact produced.
- Regression rule wired to Alertmanager -> PagerDuty and creates a GitHub issue template with run artifacts attached.

Design decisions and trade-offs: 
- Use a multi-process Python harness (asyncio) for client emulation to leverage existing test tooling; critical hot paths will be written in Rust only if Python cannot meet driver scale. This keeps iteration fast for test scenarios.
- Store per-connection minimal state (id, seed, last-token-ts) to reduce driver memory; detailed traces are sampled (1%) to keep storage costs manageable.
- Heatmaps will be generated from aggregated per-second counters sent to Prometheus; high-resolution CSV exports can be turned on for targeted runs.
- For regression detection, we will use a rolling median + MAD (median absolute deviation) rather than mean/SD to be robust to occasional noisy runs.

Implementation plan: 
1) Spec harness proto and API (config JSON) + Confluence doc.
2) Implement client patterns (short/med/long turns, multi-utterance flows) and token pacing engine (Markov-based turn length distribution).
3) Add KV-cache priming hooks and model/sequence-length tagging.
4) Add backpressure injection primitives: delayed reads, random slow-client % and TCP-emulated windowing.
5) Wire metrics: tokens/sec, bytes/sec, per-token p50/p95/p99, first-byte latency, session completion.
6) Heatmap exporter + Grafana dashboard templates.
7) Regression detection runner + Alertmanager integration + GitHub issue autopopulation.
8) Run scale validation and cost/infra runbook.

Risks and mitigation: 
- Driver scale might require horizontal sharding; mitigate with Kubernetes Job-based sharding and ephemeral instance pool.
- Prometheus scrape cardinality explosion; mitigate by using aggregated metrics and sampling for per-connection detail.
- False positives in regression alerts from infra flakiness; mitigate with repeated-run confirmation and use of robust statistics.

Runbook and infra: 
- Staging cluster tag: staging/stream-load-2026. Drivers run on k8s nodepool `load-harness-v2` (m5-like).
- Storage: artifacts to S3 bucket `s3://redwood-ci-load-artifacts/stream-heatmaps/` with TTL 30d.
- Dashboards: Grafana folder "Load/Streaming Heatmaps" (dashboard id TBD).

Links and artifacts: 
- Spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Heatmap+Streaming+Prober+Spec 
- Draft dashboard (proto): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/stream-heatmap/proto-heatmap
- Example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-load-harness/pull/421
- Baseline run artifacts (sample): https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/buckets/redwood-ci-load-artifacts/stream-heatmaps/2026-02-14-run-09/

Notes for reviewers: 
- Review focus: metrics tagging scheme (model, region, client-pattern), and the regression thresholding logic.
- Performance reviewers should validate that the token pacing engine matches production token emission histograms (sample datasets in S3).

Next steps: 
- Review spec with runtime and observability (scheduled 2026-02-25).
- Prototype driver (alpha) to be ready for internal smoke runs by 2026-03-10.
